title: Yellowface
author: R.F. Kuang
summary: June Hayward, a struggling novelist, is present when a more successful and celebrated writer dies suddenly. She walks away with an unpublished manuscript and passes it off as her own, and the lie begins to snowball.
readIf: you like sharp, biting satire of publishing and a narrator you can't fully trust.
skipIf: you need likeable characters, or want a sincere look at the book world instead of a pointed one.

pairings.reason: Another twisty, darkly funny thriller narrated by someone who bends the truth to their advantage.
A literary slide from small compromise into disaster, narrated by someone watching themselves cross lines.
Same author, historical academic fantasy that tackles power and exploitation with far less irony.
